tei:bibl.tei:title: ‎אַ דִין־תּוֹרָה מיט גאָט
A Lawsuit with God, the ḳaddish prayer of Rebbi Levi Yitsḥaq of Berditchev in Yiddish, Hebrew, and English (ca. 18th c.)
tei:bibl.tei:author: Levi Yitsḥaq Derbarmdiger Rosakov of Berditchev
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: This is “A Din Torah Mit Gott,” the Ḳaddish prayer of Rebbi Levi Yitsḥaq of Berditchev (1740-1810), in Yiddish with Hebrew, and English translations. Paul Robeson sang an adaptation of this prayer throughout his career and famously at his comeback concert at Carnegie Hall in 1958 after having been blacklisted in the early years of the Cold War (Cf. Jonathan Karp’s “Performing Black-Jewish Symbiosis: The “Hassidic Chant” of Paul Robeson“). The text of the Yiddish and Hebrew is adapted from the various nusḥaot provided at Zemereshet. The Hebrew mainly from Sefer haḤasidut (Warsaw: Di Welt 1922), p. 257-258. The Yiddish as transcribed by Yigal Landsman as his father, Hillel Landsman heard it from his father. –Aharon Varady
